speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a dermatological condition with potential oncologic implications; to begin our assessment, can you describe the appearance, size, and how long you have had any skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of heavy smoking and the description of non-healing, crusty lesions on both your penis and finger, are these lesions ulcerated, bleeding easily, or changing in size and color?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penis and Digit).

The combination of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions in a heavy smoker with a history of unsuccessful syphilis/eczema treatment is highly suspicious for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Given the potential for metastasis and the need for staging, I am requesting images of the affected sites immediately.

REQUEST IMAGES: Penis and left middle finger.
